title: Cercospora Leaf spot on Green grams

Prevention: Plant resistant and disease free seeds from
Intercrop with tall growing cereals like maize and sorghum to avoid transmission between rows.
Practice crop rotation with non- host plants such as maize.
Remove all volunteers to reduce the incidence of the disease as it can survive in soil on plant material.
Plant early to prevent damage of floral structures.
Mulch plants to avoid transmission of fungi to lower leaves.
Avoid working in the field when plants are wet.
Monitoring: Look out for leaves showing small, brown, water soaked, circular spots surrounded with yellowish halo which turn necrotic (dark brown) with reddish brown margins.
Check for infection on older leaves as severe leaf spotting can lead to heavy defoliation during flowering and pod formation.
Take action when spots first appear (30-40 days after sowing).
Direct Control: Ensure good field hygiene by removing all plant residues and burn them.
Remove and destroy the old plants and weeds to reduce disease incidence.
Space the plants about 2-3 feet apart to optimize aeration.
Apply 2 tablespoon (20 g) of 70% neem oil in 4 litres of water to reduce disease severity.
